install.adminer.description: Adminer (all-languages build, includes a Polish UI switch) - a single-file database tool covering MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MS SQL and Oracle out of the box - no need to install phpMyAdmin just to reach MariaDB. A MongoDB plugin is downloaded automatically, but MongoDB won't actually work until you also enable the pecl-mongodb module for PHP 8.3 (Services -> PHP 8.3 -> PHP Modules) - that's a deliberate manual step, since PHP extensions are shared by the whole PHP-FPM service, not just Adminer. packages.title: Hosting packages
packages.description: Define resource limits for hosting plans (disk, RAM, CPU, domains, databases). Disk and RAM limits are enforced automatically when an account is created/edited (see the "Hosting accounts" tab) - the CPU limit is defined but not yet enforced against accounts.
packages.cpu_hint: = {total}% total (with {count} cores detected on this server)
packages.resources_description: Parent CPU limit (hosting.slice) for all packages combined, so a reserve is always kept for the system, plus the quota package status (disk limits). Requires sudo permissions set up via refresh-sudoers.sh.
packages.quota_help_body: Installing the package alone (dnf install -y quota) doesn't enforce anything yet - you need to enable quota support on the target filesystem, and that depends on the disk layout of your VPS, so we don't do it automatically. First check what filesystem you actually have: findmnt -no FSTYPE,OPTIONS / (or the path where client sites live) - then use the matching example below.
packages.quota_help_xfs_title: XFS (default on AlmaLinux/Rocky) - project quota, per directory, no separate UID per site needed:
packages.quota_help_xfs_example:
1. Add prjquota in /etc/fstab (mount options column):
   UUID=xxxx-xxxx  /  xfs  defaults,prjquota  0 0

2. Mount it fresh (XFS only turns quota accounting on at mount
   time, never via remount - this is a hard XFS limitation):
   - separate partition (e.g. /home): umount /home && mount /home
   - root (/): fstab ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH. Root gets mounted by
     initramfs/dracut before systemd ever reads fstab, so the final
     mount still ends up noquota. You must add prjquota at the
     kernel/bootloader level:
       grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="rootflags=pquota"
       reboot
     Keep prjquota in fstab too (needed for normal mounting),
     grubby is an extra required step only for root.

2a. After reboot, verify it actually took effect (for / it must
    show prjquota/pquota, NOT noquota):
      cat /proc/cmdline          # must contain rootflags=pquota
      findmnt -no OPTIONS /      # must contain prjquota
      xfs_quota -x -c 'state' /  # Accounting/Enforcement: ON

That's everything you need to do by hand (one-time, for the whole
filesystem) - confirm it with the Apply button above. The entry in
/etc/projects, the entry in /etc/projid, and the xfs_quota
project/limit for each account are set automatically by the panel
when you create a hosting account (see the "Hosting accounts" card)
- don't do that part by hand.
packages.quota_help_ext4_title: ext4 - classic quota per system user:
packages.quota_help_ext4_example:
1. Add usrquota,grpquota in /etc/fstab (mount options column):
   UUID=xxxx-xxxx  /  ext4  defaults,usrquota,grpquota  0 1

2. Remount:
   mount -o remount /

3. Build the quota database:
   quotacheck -cug /

4. Turn quota on:
   quotaon /

That's everything you need to do by hand (one-time, for the whole
filesystem) - confirm it with the Apply button above. The per-user
limit (setquota) is set automatically by the panel when you create
an account in the "Hosting accounts" card - don't do that part by
hand.

5. Check:
   repquota /
packages.field_disk_fs: Disk quota mechanism (global for the VPS)
packages.field_disk_fs_hint: Requires the one-time manual setup from the example above (fstab + quotacheck/quotaon for ext4, or fstab for XFS) - only then will new accounts below actually get their package's diskQuotaMb enforced. IMPORTANT: this value must be a real, SEPARATE filesystem mount point, not an arbitrary directory - check with 'findmnt <path>' first. A plain /home directory living on the root filesystem (no partition of its own) is NOT a separate mount - in that case set this to '/' instead of '/home'.

packages.pkg_form_quota_unverified_hint: Selected mechanism: {mode} on {mount}, but NOT VERIFIED - go to "System resources" and click Apply, otherwise creating accounts with this package will be blocked.
accounts.title: Hosting accounts
accounts.description: System users with SSH access (home directory always under /home/<name>, ~/domains -> Caddy site configs). Temporary password for every new account: "PassWord!1234" - must be changed on first SSH login. The assigned package's disk limit is applied automatically on creation, through the quota mechanism selected in the section above (if set to "None", the account is created without an enforced limit) - the mount point in that section applies ONLY to the quota mechanism, not to where the home directory lives. The package's RAM limit is also applied automatically (via a systemd user-<uid>.slice) - this is the account's TOTAL memory cap across all of its processes.
accounts.no_packages: Add at least one package below (in the "Hosting packages" section) first, so there's something to assign to a new account.
accounts.confirm_delete: Remove account "{name}"? The system user will be deleted (userdel), but the home directory and data will REMAIN on disk.
mail.title: Mail
mail.not_installed_hint: Not installed. Install it from the Installer (MAIL SERVER).
mail.postfix_limits_confirm: Change Postfix limits? This writes the values to main.cf and reloads Postfix.
mail.dovecot_limits_connections_label: Max simultaneous IMAP connections per user from one IP
mail.dovecot_limits_invalid: Enter an integer of 1 or more.
mail.dovecot_limits_confirm: Change Dovecot's connection limit? This saves the value and reloads Dovecot.
mail.domain_description: Adds the detected domain to Postfix's mydestination - every local system account then becomes reachable as user@that_domain, the same mechanism as the already-working user@localhost.
mail.domain_confirm_add: Add {domain} to Postfix's mydestination? This saves the change and reloads Postfix - every local system account (not just the admin) becomes reachable as user@{domain}.
mail.admin_address_description: Purely informational - the ready-to-use address appears once the domain is added in the tile next to this one.
mail.admin_address_not_ready: Add the domain first (tile next to this one).
mail.dkim_manage_description: Manage DKIM signing for your mail domains.
mail.dkim_installed_hint: DKIM key generated and wired into OpenDKIM.
mail.dkim_not_installed_hint: No DKIM key for this domain yet - outgoing mail from it isn't signed.
mail.dkim_dns_hint: Add the record below at your DNS provider (e.g. Cloudflare):
mail.dkim_confirm_install: Install/check DKIM for {domain}? If no key exists yet, one will be generated (RSA 2048, selector "mail") and wired into OpenDKIM.
mail.spf_dns_hint: Record at the domain root - authorizes this server's real public IP as a mail sender. Nothing to install server-side, it's just a DNS entry.
mail.dmarc_dns_hint: Starts at p=none (monitoring only, no reject/quarantine) - the recommended safe first step. Aggregate reports go to dmarc@<domain>.
mail.access_limit_note: Limit per website: 2 mailboxes and 10 aliases/forwards
mail.limit_invalid: Invalid value - enter an integer of 0 or more.
mail.confirm_disable: Disable mail access for {account}? The user will lose the ability to log into the mailbox (IMAP); SSH access stays unchanged.
mail.tls_confirm_enable: Switch Postfix/Dovecot to the Let's Encrypt certificate? This copies the file from Caddy's certificate store, updates both services' config, and reloads them.
mail.tls_confirm_disable: Restore the temporary self-signed certificate on Postfix/Dovecot?
mail.stats_cert_available: Detected a trusted Let's Encrypt certificate for {host} - it can be used for Postfix/Dovecot.
mail.virtual_description: Hosting client domains, independent from the panel's system/SSH accounts - each has its own mailboxes, aliases, and DKIM.
mail.sni_description: A dedicated Let's Encrypt TLS certificate for this domain (Postfix/Dovecot) - requires Caddy to have already issued a certificate for it.
mail.sni_not_applicable: Only applies to "mail.<domain>" domains - this domain isn't one.
mail.sni_not_enabled: Mail support isn't enabled for this site - enable it in the site's settings under the Sites tab.
mail.sni_refresh_hint: The certificate renews automatically in Caddy, but you need to manually click "Refresh SNI" here so the new version reaches Postfix/Dovecot.
mail.sni_confirm_remove: Remove the SNI certificate for {domain}? It will fall back to the default certificate.
mail.virtual_confirm_remove: Remove virtual domain {domain}? All its mailboxes and aliases must be removed first.
mail.virtual_add_domain_select_empty: No sites without virtual mail yet - add a site in the Sites tab first.
mail.virtual_password_too_short: Password must be at least 8 characters.
mail.virtual_confirm_remove_mailbox: Remove mailbox {mailbox}? Existing mail stays on disk, but the account disappears from Postfix/Dovecot.
mail.virtual_prompt_source: Source login (part before @, in this domain):
mail.postfwd_description: postfwd - caps the sending rate for EACH authenticated account separately (protects against a compromised account mass-spamming through this server, which could get the whole IP blacklisted).
mail.postfwd_confirm_install: Install postfwd and wire the sending rate limit into Postfix? Defaults: 20/minute, 180/hour, 900/day per account.
mail.postfwd_invalid: Invalid value - enter whole numbers of 1 or more.
mail.postfwd_confirm_save: Save the new sending limits? The postfwd service will be restarted.
mail.antispam_description: Rejects senders without PTR/A records, requires a valid HELO, and checks the Spamhaus blacklists (zen/dbl) - pure config, no new services. Our own authenticated hosting accounts are never subject to these checks.
mail.antispam_confirm_disable: Disable Postfix anti-spam protection? The server will go back to accepting mail without these checks.
mail.spamassassin_description: Analyzes the content of every message (spamd + spamass-milter). Messages scoring above the threshold below are rejected at SMTP time, lower-scoring ones just get X-Spam-* headers (SpamAssassin's own tagging threshold stays at its default 5.0).
mail.spamassassin_confirm_install: Install SpamAssassin (spamd + spamass-milter) and wire it into Postfix? Default reject threshold: 12.
mail.spamassassin_invalid: Invalid value - enter a whole number of 1 or more.
mail.spamassassin_confirm_save: Save the new reject threshold? The spamass-milter service will be restarted.
